Classic Munro days, hand-picked. Distance, climb and time are rough estimates that allow for a walk in from the road; check the route on a map before you go.

Classic rounds are hand-picked. Mapped routes come from OpenStreetMap, where volunteers and groups like the National Trust record walking routes. A route counts a Wainwright if it passes within 60 m of the summit. Distance and climb are worked out from height data; times use Naismith's rule (5 km an hour plus an hour per 600 m of climb) and run up to a third longer to allow for breaks. GPX files save inside a .zip: unzip and import the .gpx into AllTrails, OS Maps or another app. Walks drop off this list once you've done every Wainwright on them.

Getting a GPX out of your app
  • AllTrailsOn the website, open the recording or map, then Download route and pick GPX.
  • OS MapsOpen the route, choose the export or download option and save as GPX.
  • StravaOpen the activity on the website, click the ⋯ menu and Export GPX.
  • Garmin ConnectOpen the activity, click the gear icon and Export to GPX.

None of these apps let other apps read your activities directly, so a GPX file is the way in. Menu names move around between app versions.
